originals: Is D2 skippable?
The dead android's regulator is offered only after sparing the pump android
Can Markus take the dead android's regulator before ever meeting the living one,
entries.answer: Yes: the dead android near the slope supplies a regulator even if Markus never found the living one. PowerPyx implies the new eye is used to find it ('You can scan the area and find another one near the slope').
entries.source: PowerPyx From the Dead: 'Find Pump Regulator in Dead Android: If you didn't kill the android in the middle of the area for its pump (or you never found it in the first place) you can also get a pump regulator from a dead android near the slope.'
entries.fix: ch11.json M03g option 4 requires: from {"fromDeadPump":"Refuse to kill for pump","fromDeadPumpReplaced":false,"fromDeadSearch.head":true} to {"fromDeadPumpReplaced":false,"fromDeadSearch.head":true}. Only if the operator wants the game's optional encounter; the current forced encounter is a documented, deliberate departure (M03g.adaptationNote 'Departures').

entries.topic: Who is male and who is female
originals: Who is who?
entries.answer: The android who begs to die is male (Sorrowful Android); the pump android is female (Begging Android). The pump part #2886 is listed as from a WE900; the benchmark names no models.
entries.source: Wiki Sorrowful_Android infobox gender=Male; Begging_Android infobox gender=Female; Optical unit / Thirium pump regulator table '#2886 ... WE900 in From the Dead'

entries.topic: What KILL takes from the begging android
originals: What does KILL take from the begging-to-die android?
entries.answer: Markus takes out his heart (thirium pump) to end him; the chart gives no part from this branch, and Markus still needs a regulator from the pump android or the dead android.
entries.source: Wiki Sorrowful_Android 'Markus takes out the android's heart, causing him to shut down'; wiki chart text (ANDROID BEGS TO DIE > REFUSE TO KILL OR KILL, no part node)
